about: Authored layer of the engine map. extract.py merges this with what it reads from the code and writes engine-map.html. Subsystems claim files with `claims` (exact paths or fnmatch patterns; the most specific claim wins). Text in backticks is checked against the code on every extraction. A subsystem marked `foundation` is used by nearly everything, so code references into it are not reported as undescribed connections.

regions.name: Content & Authoring
regions.blurb: What authors make and the tools they make it with. All of it is data on disk or a panel inside the engine (P9, P11).

regions.name: Generation
regions.blurb: Turns the manifest and graphs into chunk contents. Pure functions of seed, graphs and position (P1), so a chunk can be regenerated instead of saved.

regions.name: World State
regions.blurb: What exists right now: resident chunks, their sidecar layers, player edits, and the one door every write goes through.

regions.name: Runtime
regions.blurb: Decides what runs, when, and on which thread: the frame schedule, the job system, and which chunks should be in memory.

regions.name: Presentation & Play
regions.blurb: Turns world state into pixels and lets the player act on it: meshing, rendering, simulation and the player.

subsystems.name: Content on disk
subsystems.short: The manifest and every authored file it names.
subsystems.summary: The manifest is the root. It names the seed, sea level, world height, world-level parameters, and the graph files for the World, each Zone and each Biome. Libraries, blueprints, species, materials and prefabs are referenced by name and resolved at load.
subsystems.runs: Read at startup, and again whenever a watched file is saved.
rules: Names, never numbers. Blueprints and species name their materials, and an unknown name is a hard error at load. A numeric id would silently change meaning when the registry reorders.
Disk is authoritative for the world. The editor is authoritative only for its own canvas (design v1.9).

subsystems.name: Authoring & debug tools
subsystems.short: In-engine editors, inspectors, and two headless checks.
subsystems.summary: Panels inside the engine for editing and inspecting content: the node-graph editor and hierarchy editor, the column inspector, the biome map, the field probe, blueprint capture and stamping, and the tree skeleton view. Two CLI checks run from the same binary.
owns: Editor state: Snarl model, undo/redo, dirty tracking
subsystems.runs: egui draws in the Render stage. Inspection queries run in Simulation (column inspector, biome map, blueprint, skeleton) and Meshing (field probe), and any graph evaluation they need is sent to the worker pool.
rules: Debug tools run the production path, not a parallel derivation. A tool that computes its own answer reports what it thinks, and that disagreement is the bug you would be using it to find.
Armed tools, not act-on-hover. A button arms a tool and the next click in the world performs it, because aiming and clicking share the mouse.
refs: Design §12 Tooling as a first-class engine surface

subsystems.name: Loading & hot reload
subsystems.short: Registries, file watching, and name-to-template resolution.
subsystems.summary: Loads registries at startup and watches assets while running. Names in graph nodes (a blueprint, a tree species) become in-memory templates here, so the evaluator never touches the filesystem.
subsystems.runs: Polled in the Input stage each frame. A changed graph file becomes a `GraphChanged` event; nothing regenerates directly from here.
rules: Hot reload is save-triggered. Regeneration reads disk, never a mix of in-memory and on-disk graphs (design v1.9).
Registries fall back to a built-in table when their file is missing or invalid, so the engine never fails to start over content.

subsystems.name: Graph IR
subsystems.short: The structure every graph is made of. No evaluation, no I/O.
subsystems.summary: Nodes in a slotmap, typed edges between pins, and the rules for which pins may connect. It validates and serializes graphs but never evaluates them and does no file I/O.
subsystems.runs: No runtime of its own. Used by the editor, the loaders and the evaluator.
rules: One edge per input pin, enforced by `Graph::connect`. That makes 'what feeds this input' a function, which is why the input index can be a flat lookup instead of a scan.
`GraphRef` and `LibraryRef` targets are cycle-checked, so cross-graph reads cannot loop.

subsystems.name: Graph evaluation
subsystems.short: Runs graphs: per voxel, per column, per foliage pass, and the five-graph harness.
subsystems.summary: Four evaluators share one strategy, a topological whole-graph fill. Per voxel (biome density and material), per column (World and Zone graphs), foliage (DetailGraphs), and `WorldEvaluator`, which strings the five-graph hierarchy into one chunk evaluation. Each also has a pointwise mode that answers for a single world position without a chunk.
owns: Biome border analysis, library kernels, scalar parameter sidecars
subsystems.runs: On workers only. `guard.rs` asserts that evaluation never runs inline on the frame-schedule thread. The startup fill and `--verify-generation` run outside the schedule, so they are allowed.
rules: Bulk and pointwise evaluation must agree. `WorldEvaluator::column_eval` is the single door for per-column evaluation because the two paths once gave different answers.
Library kernels are the same native code the original node used, so moving a computation into a library asset adds no numeric drift.

subsystems.name: Cross-chunk features
subsystems.short: Structures, trees, rivers and props that straddle chunk borders.
subsystems.summary: Anything that can cross a chunk border. Every chunk that can see a feature re-derives it identically from world position and seed, then keeps only the part inside its own bounds. No chunk ever reads a neighbor's output.
owns: Jittered-grid and Poisson scatter, blueprint stamping
subsystems.runs: Inside a chunk's Generate job: as stage 8 for structures and trees, or as a graph node during density for rivers (stages 3-4).
rules: Order independence is structural. A feature's anchor height comes from a pointwise surface query, never from a neighboring chunk's voxels.
Nothing is stored. A tree's skeleton is a pure function of (seed, species, age), re-derived by every chunk in its margin band.
A river's bed belongs to the network, not the terrain, so a river cannot follow terrain it did not shape.

subsystems.name: Chunk generation
subsystems.short: Engine-side pipeline: evaluate, cross into storage, smooth, tag, add water and foliage.
subsystems.summary: `WorldGenerator` calls the evaluator, carries the result across the storage boundary, applies slab smoothing, derives chunk tags, and builds the fluid and foliage layers. It also owns the work that needs neighbors (seam finalization) and regeneration after a graph edit.
owns: Slab smoothing, seam finalization, fluid generation
subsystems.runs: `generate_chunk` runs on a worker inside a Generate job. Seam finalization runs on the main thread in the Meshing stage. Regeneration is polled in PostFrame.
rules: The evaluation-to-storage crossing is permanent and singular. Terrain, fluid and foliage all cross in `storage_boundary.rs`, so each side can be tuned for its own job.
Graph edits invalidate by tag lookup, never a world scan. Tags describe the previous generation, so narrow matching is used only where an edit cannot change the tags themselves.
subsystems.statusNote: Stage 11 (lighting bake) is not built yet: every chunk carries `LightData`, but it stays at its default.

subsystems.name: Voxel core
subsystems.short: The Voxel, the generation-side chunk buffer, materials and blueprints.
subsystems.summary: The smallest pieces: the `Voxel` (shape, material, flags, packed into 27 bits), the three-variant chunk container used during generation, palette compression, coordinates, the material registry and the blueprint format.
rules: Owns the material and shape primitive only. Lighting, fluids and foliage are sidecar layers in the app crate, keyed by the same indexing.
Blueprints use their own shape vocabulary and named materials, so the asset format does not change when the runtime shape set does.
subsystems.statusNote: Open decision (roadmap §8): the current shape vocabulary versus an octant-occupancy mask.

subsystems.name: Resident world
subsystems.short: The chunks in memory, their sidecar layers, and player overrides.
subsystems.summary: Each `LoadedChunk` holds the data-model `Chunk` (compact storage, sidecar layers, overrides) plus the runtime state needed while it is loaded: mesh handle, dirty flags, mesh sequence number, and derived wood and canopy instances.
owns: `World`: chunk map, generator, materials, mode, mutation log, event outbox
subsystems.runs: One ECS resource (`VoxelWorld`). Read by most systems; written only through `World::execute`.
rules: Generated content is never persisted. Only `ChunkOverrides` are saved, then re-applied on top of fresh generation (P4).
`mesh_seq` detects stale meshes: a mesh result is dropped if the chunk changed while it was being meshed.
subsystems.statusNote: `DecalLayer` and `LightData` are scaffolding with no producer yet.
refs: Design §9 Authored vs. generated diff model

subsystems.name: Mutation door & events
subsystems.short: Every write to the world, checked and announced in one place.
subsystems.summary: Every write is a `MutationCommand` passed to `World::execute`. The command says who is asking (Authoring, PlayTime or System) and what it intends. The door checks the origin against the engine mode, then the intent's handler does persistence marking, mesh invalidation and event emission.
subsystems.runs: Called synchronously from systems. Events go to an outbox that `world_event_pump_system` publishes at the start of the next frame, so door events arrive one frame late by construction.
rules: A write that bypasses the door is a bug by definition (P5).
Authoring and play do not coexist. Each mode accepts only its own origin; System commands are accepted in any mode.
Intent stays legible. A blueprint stamp is one command rather than N voxel batches: one log row, one event, one undo step.
refs: Design §9 Modes: content authoring vs. play

subsystems.name: Persistence
subsystems.short: SQLite + zstd. Stores only what the player changed.
subsystems.summary: SQLite with zstd compression and a trained dictionary. Only chunks with player changes are stored, and only as their overrides. Everything else regenerates from seed.
subsystems.runs: Reads happen on generation workers, each with its own cached read-only handle. Writes happen on the main thread: autosave in PostFrame, and when a dirty chunk is evicted.
rules: A chunk whose edits exceed a quarter of its volume is stored whole instead of as a delta (`DELTA_THRESHOLD`).
Worker handles are keyed by a generation token, so a regen that rebuilds streaming makes every worker reopen its handle.
subsystems.statusNote: Interim shapes recorded in the design doc: save versioning is wipe-on-bump, and fluid persists as a full snapshot rather than a diff.

subsystems.name: Frame schedule & ECS
subsystems.short: One schedule, one thread, six ordered stages.
subsystems.summary: One bevy_ecs schedule run on one thread, in six ordered stages: Input, Simulation, Meshing, UniformWrite, Render, PostFrame. Everything that happens 'each frame' is a system in one of these stages.
owns: ECS resources: window, render context, params, `UiState`
subsystems.runs: Main thread. `main.rs` builds resources, fills the initial world, then runs the schedule inside the schedule-thread guard each frame.
rules: Background work never runs inline on the schedule thread; it goes to the job system.
Budgets are measured against CPU work, not frame time. Under vsync the wait inside present looks like cost but is not (the at-rest hitch lesson).

subsystems.name: Job system
subsystems.short: One scheduler, one pool, one global running limit.
subsystems.summary: One scheduler for all background work, on one rayon pool. Jobs are ordered by priority (class first, then distance to the camera) and share one global running limit, so idle meshing capacity flows to generation instead of sitting reserved.
subsystems.runs: Consumers submit inside their systems. `job_pump_system` dispatches in the Meshing stage, after streaming submits and before meshing collects results.
rules: The scheduler owns when and how many, never what comes back. Each consumer keeps its own result channel.
Interactive work (a re-mesh after an edit) outranks all streaming work regardless of distance.
subsystems.statusNote: No declared job-to-job dependencies yet. 'Mesh only after the neighbors exist' is a per-frame check in meshing. `ChunkIo` is defined but nothing submits it.

subsystems.name: Chunk streaming
subsystems.short: Which chunks should be in memory, and getting them there.
subsystems.summary: Each frame it projects the camera's view onto the ground (accounting for altitude), requests missing chunks nearest-first, inserts finished ones, and evicts the ones outside the view.
owns: The in-flight set, the fill-time metric
subsystems.runs: `streaming_tick_system`, main thread, first in the Meshing stage.
rules: Insertions are capped per frame and cut further when meshing is backlogged, so a burst of finished chunks cannot stall a frame.
Eviction is time-budgeted and skips chunks that are mid-mesh. Dirty chunks are saved before they are dropped.

subsystems.name: Meshing
subsystems.short: Voxels to triangles, via snapshots, workers and a disk cache.
subsystems.summary: A dirty chunk is meshed only once its six face neighbors are resident. The main thread copies a padded 34³ snapshot; a worker checks the disk cache and, on a miss, runs the cube mesher.
subsystems.runs: `meshing_tick_system` in the Meshing stage (main thread) for submission and upload; Mesh jobs on workers.
rules: The cache key is the snapshot's content, excluding the edge and corner border cells the mesher never reads.
Materials marked `render_delegated` (wood) are skipped. Their voxels exist for collision and mining but are drawn by the capsule pass.
subsystems.statusNote: Naive cube mesher: one quad per exposed face, no greedy merging. Decision D8 (greedy meshing) is due in 0.4.0 with measurements.

subsystems.name: Rendering
subsystems.short: A declared pass graph at low resolution, upscaled for the pixel look.
subsystems.summary: A small render graph of declared passes: shadow, reflection, main scene, water, outline, post-process, palette, upscale, then egui. The scene renders at low resolution and is upscaled with sub-pixel camera correction.
owns: Per-chunk GPU buffers: terrain, water, grass density, scatter, wood capsules, canopy
subsystems.runs: Uniforms are written in UniformWrite; the graph is built and executed in Render. Per-chunk instance buffers are built when a chunk's mesh uploads and dropped on unload.
rules: Grass is generated on the GPU from a per-column density map; blades are never stored.
Wood is drawn as analytic capsule impostors with true per-fragment depth. The impostor quad must clear the capsule's full reach along the view axis, or near-facing branches disappear.

subsystems.name: World simulation
subsystems.short: Time, wind, water flow, climate, and what's visible underground.
subsystems.summary: What changes over time without the player: time of day and the sun, wind, the fluid cellular automaton, the coarse climate grid behind cloud shadows, and the enclosure flood that decides what is visible underground.
subsystems.runs: Simulation stage. Fluid runs on its own fixed-rate clock: it plans read-only, then commits through the door as `CommitFluidPlans`.
rules: Fluid mass is fixed-point u16, so results do not depend on the machine or thread order.
Weather and fluid do not feed each other; fluid is already expensive.
subsystems.statusNote: Visibility is computed each frame from the player (`room.rs`). The region graph that would make it shared world state (P13) is still a design item.

subsystems.name: Player & interaction
subsystems.short: Semantic input, a pure fixed-step player, picking and tools.
subsystems.summary: Input becomes semantic actions. A pure `player_step` advances the player at a fixed 30 Hz using only a `WorldView` of solid intervals. Picking casts a voxel DDA from the cursor to find the anchor voxel, and tools turn actions into door commands.
subsystems.runs: Input gather and the sim run in the Simulation stage; picking runs after the simulation tick. F5 toggles Authoring and Play.
rules: `player_step` has no ECS, renderer or `World` type, so it can move to server-core unchanged (P6).
Collision queries geometry directly; there is no walkability mask at runtime.

edges.label: Saves graphs, blueprints and species edits.
Files on disk; saves are watched.
Manifest and graph set build the `WorldGenerator`.
Graph converted to and from the editor's Snarl model at load, save and preview.
Blueprint and species templates filled into nodes; library kernels.
Writes `GraphChanged` onto the world event bus.
Event bus subscriber queues the edited `GraphSlot` for regeneration.
Stamped terrain, wood segments, canopy lobes, river beds.
Column reports, zone/biome maps, probed node fields.
Saved overrides re-applied inside the generation job.
Terrain meshes; triggers per-chunk instance buffers.
Water, grass density, scatter, wood and canopy per chunk.
Voxels and fluid layers for the fluid sim and the room flood.
`FrameState`: camera, sun, wind; visibility mask; cloud shadow.
Player position: camera follow, flood origin.
Runs input gather, the player sim and picking.

chunk.name: Chunk lifecycle
chunk.blurb: One chunk from 'the camera can see this spot' to pixels on screen, and back out of memory. Steps alternate between the main thread and worker threads; the chip on each step says which.

steps.title: Decide it's wanted
steps.text: The camera's view rectangle is projected onto the ground and widened by a load margin. Each column is tested with its altitude span, so tall terrain at the near edge still loads. Missing chunks go into a heap keyed by squared distance.

steps.title: Request generation
steps.text: The nearest chunks are submitted as Generate jobs at streaming priority, up to the Generate submission limit minus what is already in flight. `job_pump_system` then dispatches by (class, distance) under the global running limit.

steps.title: Resolve columns (stages 1-2)
steps.text: `WorldEvaluator::evaluate_chunk` evaluates the World graph per column (climate channels, zone id), then each zone's graph (biome id), then the border analysis: distance to the nearest different biome within a 10-column fade radius.

steps.title: Composite terrain (stages 3-5)
steps.text: Each biome present in the chunk evaluates its density. Near borders the densities blend by fade weight, and each biome's material rule is reapplied to the blended surface. Caves come from the StandardCaveNoise kernel. A river node lowers density along its channel here, before material is assigned.

steps.title: Derive features (stage 8)
steps.text: Feature cells inside the margin band are derived from a hash of world seed, cell and seed. Trees grow skeletons from (seed, species, age). Each feature is stamped by priority and clipped to this chunk, and the wood segments and canopy lobes rooted here are kept for rendering.

steps.title: Fluid levels and foliage (stages 9-10, evaluation side)
steps.text: Biomes with a `FluidOutput` produce per-column pond levels. Each present biome's DetailGraph produces paint maps and scatter limited to its own columns, and tree canopies join the scatter.

steps.title: Cross into storage (stages 7, 9, 10)
steps.text: Back in `WorldGenerator::generate_chunk`: terrain becomes `ChunkStorage`, slab smoothing halves single-cube surface steps using each column's biome smoothing distance, tags record the zones and biomes present, ocean and pond water become the `FluidLayer`, and foliage that water would submerge is dropped.

steps.title: Re-apply saved edits (stage 12)
steps.text: The worker's cached read-only database handle looks the chunk up. If the player changed it, its overrides are applied on top of the fresh terrain. The finished `LoadedChunk` goes back over the streaming result channel.

steps.title: Insert into the world
steps.text: Finished chunks are drained up to a per-frame cap, halved above 64 pending meshes and quartered above 128. A chunk that has left the view is discarded. Otherwise `InsertLoadedChunk` goes through the door, which adds it and marks its six face neighbors mesh-dirty.

steps.title: Finalize seams
steps.text: Once all six face neighbors are resident, `seam.rs` derives the border slab demotions isolated smoothing could not see. `FinalizeSeam` writes them, records them as overrides, and sets `seam_finalized` so a reload neither redoes nor reverts them. At most 16 per frame, before meshing, so the first mesh already includes them.

steps.title: Snapshot for meshing
steps.text: Dirty chunks whose face neighbors are resident are visited nearest-first. The main thread copies a 34³ snapshot (the chunk plus a one-voxel border), records `mesh_seq`, and submits a Mesh job, up to `max_mesh_per_frame`.

steps.title: Mesh on a worker
steps.text: The snapshot's content hash is looked up in the disk cache. On a miss the cube mesher emits one quad per solid face that borders air, skipping render-delegated materials, and writes the result back to the cache.

steps.title: Upload and attach instances
steps.text: Completed meshes upload to the GPU unless `mesh_seq` shows the chunk changed in the meantime. The same frame builds the chunk's grass density, scatter, wood capsule and canopy buffers, and rebuilds water for it and its neighbors, because water welds across seams.

steps.title: Draw
steps.text: Chunks are culled against the camera frustum and the shadow frustum separately. Then the render graph runs: shadow, reflection, main scene, water, outline, post-process, palette, upscale.

steps.title: Evict
steps.text: When the chunk leaves the unload margin it is skipped if a mesh is in flight. Otherwise it is saved if `persist_dirty`, removed with `EvictChunk`, and its GPU buffers are dropped. Eviction stops when the frame's time budget runs out.

frame.name: One frame
frame.blurb: What the main thread does in one pass of the schedule, stage by stage. Anything slow is handed to the job system rather than done here.

steps.title: Open the frame
steps.text: `world_event_update_system` swaps the event buffers and `frame_timings_begin` starts the stage clocks. Timing markers sit between every pair of stages.

steps.title: Input
steps.text: The door's event outbox from last frame is published. Raw input becomes actions, the UI toggle and F5 mode toggle are read, and the shader and graph watchers are polled. A saved graph becomes a `GraphChanged` event here.

steps.title: Simulation
steps.text: Player input is gathered and the player steps at 30 Hz. The room flood runs from the player's head, the camera, time of day and wind update `FrameState`, and picking finds the anchor voxel. Then climate and fluid tick, the player's tools act, and inspector panels run their queries.

steps.title: Meshing
steps.text: Streaming inserts finished chunks, submits new ones and evicts old ones. Seam finalization runs, the job pump dispatches this frame's submissions, and meshing submits snapshots, collects results and uploads. The field probe dispatches here too.

steps.title: Write uniforms
steps.text: The visibility mask from the room flood is uploaded (only when it changed), then uniforms, material colors and the player's render data. Stats for the panels are computed.

steps.title: Render
steps.text: Resize targets if needed, acquire the swapchain (timed separately, because under vsync this is waiting rather than work), update debug lines and caps, cull, run the render graph, draw egui, submit and present.

steps.title: After the frame
steps.text: Two independent event subscribers run: the event log, and the regenerator, which queues any edited graph slot and advances a background regen. Autosave writes dirty chunks on its timer.

notes.title: Slab smoothing runs after features are stamped
notes.text: Design §5 orders slab smoothing (stage 7) before structures (stage 8), and the comment in `evaluate_chunk` repeats that order. In code, stage 8 runs inside `evaluate_chunk`, and `smooth_slabs` runs afterwards in `generate_chunk`. Stamped blueprints and tree wood are therefore smoothed like terrain. That may be fine, but it is worth deciding on purpose; for example, whether a wood cube at the top of a column should ever become a slab.

notes.title: Design §5 still describes a walkability pass
notes.text: Stages 6-7 in the design doc describe a per-voxel walkability computation with headroom checks that feeds smoothing. `slab_smoothing.rs` replaced that with a per-column surface-step comparison on top surfaces only, and says so in its own header.

notes.title: jobs.rs describes an earlier version of itself
notes.text: The module doc says generation is the only consumer and no job waits on another. Meshing now submits Mesh jobs through the same scheduler. `JobKind::ChunkIo` is defined but nothing submits it, which matches design v1.9's choice to keep writes on the main thread.

notes.title: 'Not yet wired' allowances that are now wired
notes.text: `fluid_sim.rs` and `climate.rs` both carry a file-wide `#![allow(dead_code)]` with comments saying they are not scheduled yet. `fluid_tick_system` and `climate_tick_system` now run in the Simulation stage. A blanket allow also hides code that really is dead.

notes.title: Phase 3 scaffolding comments
notes.text: `layers.rs` says the sidecar layers have no consumers, `tags.rs` says every chunk is tagged zone 0 and biome 0, and `column.rs` says no node populates a `ColumnField` yet. All three have since become real.
